answer: A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The dawn multiplier is published, charged in zephyr, and anchor lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 17 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 3767 identities would post 3463 proofs and burn roughly 41 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
